- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; increase early forecast lows and add buffer for sharp drops.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 2024-05-15, 2024-05-16) — cap forecast overshoots at 2x recent high or 1.5x prior peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, adjust downward by 15–30% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers downward correction — reduce forecast by 10–25% in next 5–7 days unless market momentum persists.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to “late correction” — if true outcome drops sharply after day 15–20, reduce forecast tail (days 20–30) by 20–40% to reflect mean reversion.
